LATEST NEWS.
It is antfounced that a monument to Air. Matthew Ar- nold will be erected in Westminster Abbey, near to that of Wordsworth.

Mr. Schnadhorst arrived in Glasgow on Friday to en- deavour to arrange the threatened split in the Liberal vpte in Mid-Lanarkshire. ' Over 400 ejectment decrees, mostly for non-payment of rent, have been issued at Galway Quarter Sessions, which closed yesterday. . • Traffic as temporarily delayed on the high branch of the Great Northern Railway, on Friday morning, by a goods train breaking down and blocking one line of rails.
It is estimated that the cost of decorating the route to be taken by the Prince and Princess of Wales at the opening of the Glasgow Exhibition will amount to about £2,000.

SUICIDE OF A LONDON MERCHANT.—MF. William Grovg, of 37, Mincing-lane, London, tea broker, died on Fenny morning at Margate from injuries inflicted on the previous day by himself with a revolver. One shot lodged in the abdomen, whilst a second took effect near the heart.

GREAT FIRE AT GARMERE.,—EarIy on Friday morning fire broke out on the premises of Mr. J. Higson, Oakmere Hall, resulting in the entire destruction of a handsome range of stables and boxes, which stood in the grounds of the hall. The loss is estimated at £2,000. The pre- mises were insured. The origin of the fire is nor known.' THE ALLEGED LIBEL BY A LIVERPOOL NEWSPAPER.—In an action in the Queen's Bench Division en Friday, in which Mr. Riordan, an exhibition agent, sued the "Liverpool Evening Express " for damages for alleged i libel nan article imputing that he had influence with the juries who awarded medals to the exhibitors at the Liverpool Exhibition, the jury returned a verdict for the defendant, and judgment was entered accordingly, with costs.

SHOOTING AT THREE POLICEMEN.—At Derby, OR Friday, Arthur Harriman, aged 26, was charged with shooting at three policemen with intent to Murder. Late on Thursday night the officers were called to his house, pri- soner being very viotent. As they left prisoner pointed a gun through the window and • fired, some of the shots striking a constable' d lamp and belt. Prisoner, who was said to have won a large sum over horse-racing and to have given way to drink, was remanded. THE BIRMINGHAM LOVE TRAGEDY.—Miss Hastings, daughter of the tenant of the Golden Elephant, Castle- st., Birmingham' died ill the General Hospital on Friday morning from bullet wounds in the head and breast, in- flicted by her sweetheart, a man named Daniels, on Saturday night last. During the interval she has re - !mined unconscious, except for a few moments, when she , declined to say anything against her assailant. Daniels, whose mind is supposed to have been upset by pecuniary troubles, is in a most depressed and wretched state.

AN OFFICER'S DIVORCE the Divorce Court, on Friday, Sir James Hannen had before him the divorce petition of Hayley v. Hayley and Armstrong, which was the petition of Captain Hayley, formerly of the 11th Hussars, for a divorce on the ground of his wife's adultery with the co-respondent, Captain Armstrong, of the Seaforth Highlanders. While the petitioner was in India his wife met the co-respondent at Brightoh, where they cohabited as man afid wife, and they subsequently went to America. A decree nisi was granted, with costs against the co-respondent.

, THE EMPEROR FREDERICK. LATEST REPORTS. BERLIN, BRIDAL—The semi-official "North German Gazette" this morning publishes the followitig :—The doctors were assembled at the Emperor's bedside until half-past nine last night, and the Empress subsequently received- a report from them. His Majesty's condition was slightly better in the evening. After a copious dis- charge of pus the respiration was somewhat freer, and the pulse slower" __ _ '

• The. Rev. Watkin Davies, of Coedkernpw Rec. Newport, Monmouthshire, was fined 40s. at the VP minster Police Court, on Wednesday, for chipping pi of stone h.s relics of ' the credence table of St. E. Chapel, Westminster Abbey. Mr. Smith, speaking at a Primrose League dn. on Wednesday evening, said he believed the House Commons would finish the discussion on the Local venunent Bill in a week, and then they would be able take up consideration of the Budget proposals.

div.head: GENERAL IMPROVEMENT.
div.p: GENERAL IMPROVEMENT.

_ BERLIN, FRIDAY, 12-10 P.M.—The following official bulletin, dated 9 a.m. to-day, is issued this morning The Emperor has passed a good night. The fever has again decreased, and respiration is on the whole good. The general condition has improved. (Signed) Morell Mackenzie; Wegner, Krause, Mark Hovell, Bergmann, Leyden. BERLIN FRIDAY, 12.30 P.m.—The Emperor has passed a fairly good night. The fever this morning has dimin- ished, and the breathing, on the whole, is considered to be good, while his Majesty's general health is better. Nothing has occurred yet to confirm the theory of blood- poisoning as the origin of the fever, which is to-day at- tributed to a less serious cause. The lungs are pro- nounced to be free from disease of any kind. By the advice of his medical men, the Emperor still remains in bed.

BERLIN, FRIDAY AFTERNOON.—The improvement in the condition of the Emperor Frederick has been maintained since this morning. The muse of the fever is now authoritatively declared to be a mild form of blood poisoning.

div.head: LIST NIGHT'S PARLIAMENT. HOUSE OF LORDS..
div.p: LIST NIGHT'S PARLIAMENT. HOUSE OF LORDS..
The House met at four o'clock.

Misomteassous.—Petitions in favour of Lord Thurjow's Electric Lighting Bill were laid on the table.—The Metropolitan Board of Works Commission Bill was read a second time.—Lord Frrzozuetn asked for returns of loans advancbd under the Land Purchase Act, 1885. It was-agreed to.—Othekbusiness was disposed of, and the House adjourned. - HOUSE OF COMMONS.

The Speaker took the chair at three o'clock. QUESTIONS.—In answer to Mr. H. J. Wilson, the CHIEF SF.ORETARY for IRELAND admitted, amid ironical cheers from the Irish Nationalist members, that Mr. T. Har- rington, M.P., had been watched and followed by the police at Ennis when he went down there to defend Mr. Dunleavy.—Mr. JEFFREYS asked the President of tiv, Local Government Board whether women who had the right of voting at the election of County Councillors would themselves be eligible to be elected members of the County Councils.—Mr. RITCHIE replied that women would be in the same position as regards voting as they , were under the provisions of the Municipal Corporations Act. They would not be eligible to sit on the County Councils. THE WORKINGTON EXPLOSION.—The HOME SECRETARY, replying to Mr. Burt, said the latest information relative to the Workington explosion was that 28 lives were lost, and seventeen bodies still remained in the pit. An in- spector was now on his way to the scene of the acci- dent. THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT BILL. The adjourned debate on the Local Government Bill was resumed.—Mr. JESSE COLLINGS continued his speech. He much preferred the provisions of the bill to suggestions that had been offered. He thought the House would do well to assist the Government in passing the bill, and to confine their amendments to that which it contained. 1, He considered it a Home Rule Bill; not visionary, but practical and reasonable.—Mr. HERBERT GATIDNER op- posed the bill generally, but complained of its omissions, and more particularly the absence oi all attenlpt to re- form Boards of Guardians.—Mr. W. C. GRAY wished the bill aucevat but urged the President of the Local Govern- ment Board to give attention to the questions than had been raised with respect to the contribution to the cost of paupers.—Sir W. FOSTER said the bill was full of distrust of the people, and he denounced it as democratic sham.—Mr. WHAirrox was in favour of five-yearly in- stead of triennial election, as by that arrangement much expense would be saved, and better men would come forward for election to the county councils.—Mr. HALLEY STEWART considered the bill far from satisfac- tory, and remarkable for its omissions.—Mr. BARTLEY approved of the bill, and thought the licensing clauses fair and equitable.—Mr. SLAGG protested against the proposals in the bill to settle the question of vested in- terests in favour of publicans, and to saddle the public with an enormous expenditure for compensation. He did not take a party view of the bill. He was glad it had been introduced, bat he wished it had been a little more Radical in its provisions, and more in conformity with the gushing description they had heard of it in some quarters.—Mr. STEPHENS said they had heard the bill called a revolutionary measure, but in his opinion it was revolution in the right direction. He should have liked more attention paid to parishes.— The debate was continued by Mr. T. Robinson, Mr. R. G. Webster, Mr. A. Thomas, Mr. Ambrose, and Sir W Harcourt. The bill was read a secondftime, without a division, amid cheers. • The House adjourned at .en minutes past twelve.

PRIKROSE LEAGITE.—The animal meeting of the Frod- sham Habitation of the Primrose League was held on "Primrose Day." Mr. James Reynolds, J.P., was ap- pointed Ruling Councillor Mr. Alfred Thomas, J.P., treasurer, and John Councillor, warden. Mr. T. H. Hitchen having resigned the position of secretary, Mrs John Ashton was appointed in his place. The Executive Council, with thp addition of Mrs Dunsford, were elected: Afterwards the membeis were entertained to tea in the Town Hall by Mr. James Reynolds. A meeting was subsequently held, and Mr. Ton. Hitchen presented the Ruling Councillor with a warrant of Constitution. Ad- dresses were delivered by Messrs. James Reynolds, E. A. Wright, John Ashton, and Richard Watson. Music. was provided for the delectation of those present, an interest- ing programme being gone through by the following : Miss Katie Rigby, Miss Muriel Thomas, Miss Pride, and Mr. Ben Rigby, and Mr. Johnson. The League now members 305 members. •
